No - because the original saying is "the grass is always greener on the other side of the fence". Consider that. If it's always greener on the other side of the fence that means that if you go on to the other side then suddenly the side you were in is gonna start to look greener.

It's a pretty old and well understood saying. Consider what it tells us about human nature: we have a strong tendency to look at our neighbors, friends and associates and think that they are better off (greener grass) than ourselves. But this is only because we only get to see them at their best - we don't see their daily struggles, their inner flaws, their weak moments... Much like Facebook - people don't post when they're feeling shitty and depressed so if you look at their profiles it gives off the impression they're always happy and gay.

What this quote here is telling us is a solution to this other problem. Instead of wanting to jump fences around and always be under the illusion you're last in line why don't instead we try to think about what is giving off the illusion that our neighbor is better off than we? Does he have a great marriage? If so maybe I want to talk to my wife and see if she is happy about us. Does he have a barbecue grill to invite friends over on weekends? Maybe I want to buy one myself or invite friends over to play poker on Sunday. Does everyone around think he is a great guy? Maybe I should consider if I'm treating people around me badly and driving them away...
